name: 50992-longprefill-1b-1gpu
hardware: 1x H100 80GB HBM3 (one GPU of an a3 node, --gres=gpu:1), plus 4 GiB of host DRAM used as a KV tier. No disk, no remote store, no NIC on the serving path.
architecture: LlamaForCausalLM, bf16, 1.24B parameters: 16 layers, hidden 2048, 32 query heads over 8 KV heads, head_dim 64, intermediate 8192, vocab 128256, tied embeddings, max_position_embeddings 131072.
load_profile: concurrent (closed loop), streams=1, bound at 200 requests, warmup 10% and cooldown 10%, static seed 50992.
workload: Long-prompt, short-answer, single turn, no reuse. guidellm `synthetic_text`: 32768 prompt tokens fixed (min=max), 8 output tokens fixed (min=max), temperature 0, 200 requests. Prompts are distinct row by row.
purpose: A document analysis service answering brief questions about 32-thousand-token filings, one request at a time on a single GPU.
launch:
# The engine's command line. One H100 of an a3 node, guidellm driving vLLM in-process through the
# `vllm_python` backend.

model: unsloth/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct
tensor-parallel-size: 1
max-model-len: 40960

# Equal to the prompt length, so one request's prefill is one scheduler step.
max-num-batched-tokens: 32768
block-size: 16

# The host-DRAM KV tier. KEEP IT ON ONE LINE AS JSON: the config reader is flat, so a dict written
# as an indented YAML block is silently dropped and the engine starts with no offload tier at rc=0.
kv-transfer-config: {"kv_connector": "OffloadingConnector", "kv_role": "kv_both", "kv_connector_extra_config": {"cpu_bytes_to_use": 4294967296, "eviction_policy": "arc"}}

# Off, and it is on by default in this era: it overlaps step preparation with the previous step's
# GPU work, which blurs a per-step latency, and it has been unstable on this cluster.
async-scheduling: false
